title: Monomark Engineering (India) IPO
summary: Monomark Engineering (India) IPO is a book-built issue of 2.7 crore shares, to be listed on BSE and NSE. The IPO opens on December 2, 2026 and closes on December 4, 2026, with allotment expected on December 7 and listing on December 9, 2026. The price band and lot size are yet to be announced.

Monomark Engineering (India) financials show revenue growth and profitability trends over recent years, indicating business stability.

Incorporated in 2005, Monomark Engineering (India) Limited is involved in the provision of O&M services for industrial operations, metal fabrication solutions, and industrial project execution services for clients from various sectors such as metals, cement, ports, and engineering/OEMs. · · There are two ways that Monomark Engineering implements projects; EPC and FEIC. In EPC model, the company provides end-to-end project execution services encompassing engineering, procurement, construction, erection, installation, and commissioning. FEIC model entails carrying out of on-site fabrication, erection, installation, and commissioning services while design and procurement are carried out by the client or some other contractor. · · Monomark Engineering currently has 28 active projects as of February 28, 2026, which include 20 O&M projects and 8 execution projects. The firm has executed 20 projects within the last five years across its business segments. · · The company runs its manufacturing unit at Chittorgarh, Rajasthan and maintains offices and project sites in various states of India such as Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Goa, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The company has a total employee strength of 6,381 workers, including 836 permanent and 5,545 project-based employees.
Narendra Chordia, Meena Chordia, Nitesh Chordia, Gaurav Chordia are the company's promoters of Monomark Engineering (India).

sections.h: Monomark Engineering (India) IPO - Strengths and Risks

b.p: Monomark Engineering (India) IPO strengths and risks highlight key business factors, financial position, and market sentiment that may impact investor interest.

Experienced Promoters & Qualified Manpower: With decades of experience in O&M, execution and fabrication, along with technically competent manpower that includes diploma & engineers, the promoters of the company help deliver consistent services and scalable operations.

Integrated Engineering Services Capabilities: With the integration of its various O&M, execution and metal fabrication capabilities, MEIL gives its customers the option to deal with one provider throughout the life cycle of industrial asset, and backed with 28 active projects and fleet of 232 vehicles as on September 30, 2026.
Presence in Diverse Sectors: The company has its presence in diverse sectors such as metals, cement, ports and engineering, making it easy for them to understand operations in different sectors.

Risk of Customer Concentration: 41.31% of the company’s total income comes from its only largest client, Hindustan Zinc Limited, and 91.37% of its top five clients for the period ending June 30, 2026, putting the company at risk in case of the loss of some of those clients.

Metal and Cement Sectors Dependence: The company generates 93.66% of its income from the metal and cement sectors for the period ending June 30, 2026; these two sectors are affected by many economic changes as well as recent geopolitical tensions that have affected the operations of its subsidiary in the UAE.

Industrial Operations and Maintenance Segment Dependence: The company earns 89.76% of its total income from its O&M segment for the period ending June 30, 2026; any inability to execute or maintain such contracts will affect its income substantially.
